Where to Ride: Month by Month

Britain's touring potential changes with the seasons, and the ideal destination shifts throughout the year. This month-by-month guide gives you the perfect UK motorcycle destination for every month — matching weather, daylight, scenery, and riding conditions to the best region for the time of year.

The Calendar

  • January: Cornwall coast. The mildest winter riding in Britain. Coastal roads, cream teas, and temperatures that rarely drop below 5°C.
  • February: Dorset and the New Forest. Early spring arrives in the south. Snowdrops, quiet lanes, and lengthening days.
  • March: Wye Valley and South Wales. Daffodils, sheltered valley riding, and the first warm days.
  • April: Cotswolds. Spring blossom, green fields, honey-stone villages. The quintessential English spring.
  • May: Scottish Highlands. The best month for Highland touring. No midges, long days, empty roads, stunning light.
  • June: Isle of Skye and the Outer Hebrides. Midsummer in the islands. 18 hours of daylight and magical landscapes.
  • July: Northumberland and the Scottish Borders. Warm, quiet, spectacular. Beat the Lake District and Highland crowds.
  • August: North York Moors. Heather season turns the moorland purple. Combine with the Yorkshire coast.
  • September: Lake District. The golden month. Post-summer calm, autumn light beginning, mirror-still lakes.
  • October: Perthshire and the Wye Valley. Peak autumn colour. Blazing reds, golds, and coppers.
  • November: Devon coast. Mild enough for riding, atmospheric autumn light, quiet roads.
  • December: Channel Islands (Guernsey). Mild maritime climate, festive atmosphere, compact island riding.

The Year-Round Tourer

Following this calendar, a year-round tourer covers the full breadth of British riding:

  • 12 months of riding in 12 different regions
  • Each month matched to optimal conditions
  • A progression from mild winter south to summer north and back
  • Approximately 3,000-5,000 touring miles across the year
You don't need to travel abroad to have a riding season full of variety. Britain's 12 months offer 12 distinct touring experiences — from frost-crisp January coastal rides to golden September Highland tours. The beauty is in the variety. Every month is riding season if you know where to go.

Planning Your Year

  • Book your main summer tour 3-6 months ahead (June-August)
  • Spring and autumn tours can be booked 1-2 months ahead
  • Winter rides are spontaneous — check the forecast and go
  • Use this calendar as a starting framework and adjust based on weather and personal preference

A year of UK motorcycle touring awaits. Every month offers something unique, something beautiful, and something worth riding for. The ideal region shifts through the year, following warmth north in spring and back south through autumn.
May and June are for the Highlands and islands, with long days, no midges, and empty roads.

faq.q: Which month is best for the Scottish Highlands?
faq.a: May and June. May offers the best Highland touring of the year, with long days, no midges, empty roads, and stunning light, while June extends daylight to 18 hours and adds the islands of Skye and the Outer Hebrides. Both come before the peak summer crowds and midge season worsens later.

faq.q: Where should I ride in the depths of winter?
faq.a: Head to the mildest corners. January suits the Cornwall coast, where the Gulf Stream keeps temperatures rarely below 5C, and December works well in Guernsey, whose mild maritime climate and festive atmosphere pair with compact island riding. Both let you keep riding when the rest of Britain is frozen.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book each tour?
faq.a: Book your main summer tour, June to August, three to six months ahead, as the best accommodation near popular areas disappears early. Spring and autumn tours can be booked one to two months ahead, while winter rides are best kept spontaneous: watch the forecast and go when a dry, mild window appears.

faq.q: How many miles does a year-round tourer cover?
faq.a: Following a month-by-month calendar of 12 different regions, a year-round tourer covers roughly 3,000 to 5,000 touring miles across the year. Each month is matched to optimal conditions, progressing from the mild winter south to the summer north and back, delivering 12 distinct touring experiences without ever leaving Britain.
